sources.title: [26.16] Diamond Gnar Guide - Thing in the Ice

passive.name: Rage Gene
passive.text: While in combat Gnar generates Rage. At maximum Rage his next ability will transform him into Mega Gnar, granting increased survivability and access to new spells.

spells.name: Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss
spells.text: Gnar throws a boomerang that damages and slows enemies it hits before returning to him. If he catches the boomerang its cooldown is reduced.Mega Gnar instead throws a boulder that stops on the first unit hit, damaging and slowing everything nearby. It can then be picked up to reduce the cooldown.

spells.name: Hyper / Wallop
spells.text: Gnar's attacks and spells hype him up, dealing bonus damage and granting him Move Speed.Mega Gnar is too enraged to be hyper and instead can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area.

spells.name: Hop / Crunch
spells.text: Gnar leaps to a location and bounces off the head of any unit he lands on, traveling further.Mega Gnar is too large to bounce and instead lands with earth-shattering force, dealing damage in an area around him.

spells.name: GNAR!
spells.text: Mega Gnar throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.

archetype.value: Gnar is a versatile ranged champion who plays safely at a distance and gains substantial crowd control as Mega Gnar.

axis.value: Gnar can poke from a distance but struggles when caught by gap closers.

winCondition.value: Gnar can fit into almost any team composition by combining damage, poke, mobility, crowd control, and the ability to kill tanks.

spikes.why: Gnar gains substantial crowd control, though the timing is dictated by Rage.
Gnar can trigger Hyper more often and execute a faster basic attack → Boomerang Throw → basic attack.

mistakes.value: Gnar can be forced by Rage to transform at a poor time.
